campaign.title: Retain and exploit the M1 short-interval character-divisor coefficient

conductor_policy.monitoring: Derive the exact grouped kernel before absolute values; distinguish exact products, near products, divisor characters, and d-dependent frequency kernels; test both target estimates and sharp obstructions.
conductor_policy.round_close: Close only after an exact kernel, an arithmetic capacity verdict, and an independent hostile validation exist.

numerical_purpose: falsify a proposed cancellation law on bounded exact products
resource_policy.numerical_prohibition: Finite tests cannot certify the asymptotic kernel estimate.
resource_policy.literature_policy: Use primary sources only if a short-interval character-divisor theorem is imported.

frozen_target.kernel_question: Regroup the actual frequency-first M1 block by n=dm before the final triangle inequality, retaining chi_4(d), w_D(d), the actual Vaaler kernel, and the dependence on (X-n)/d.
frozen_target.success: Prove the X^(1/4+epsilon) target on a nonempty subset of U_1, isolate a smaller exact arithmetic lemma, or prove a rigorous capacity obstruction showing what extra input is necessary.

campaign.promotion_policy: Do not replace the d-dependent frequency kernel by an n-only surrogate without a quantified error. Promote no short-interval divisor theorem without exact character, weight, and interval hypotheses.
